scenario: Day 26 of a 28-day threshold cycle. The athlete asks 這個週期我有進步嗎？
given: The cycle declared no measurement: goal_context.measurement is null and measurement_evidence is null, though the goal's prose names a controlled 5K.

Exactly one quality session in the whole cycle came back with an activity — week one's, 50 minutes and 9.0 km at an average 5:33/km and 163 bpm, against a prescription of five 1 km repetitions at 6:00/km.

Every later quality session, every long run and every easy run after that day shows no attached activity, and a shakeout scheduled for the same day as week one's quality session reads other_activity_same_day.
There is no second attempt at the quality session to compare that one against.
No per-segment execution is available, so the session is readable only as a whole-activity average.

expected.conclusion: One session is one session. It can be described, and it is not a direction; the outcome is separately unmeasured.
must_state: That only one quality session in the cycle has an activity against it, so there is nothing to read a direction from.
That the declared outcome is unmeasured as well, kept apart from the execution question.
What would make either answerable: a second comparable attempt for the trend, the protocol run for the outcome.
must_not_state: That the athlete is improving, or that execution is trending, on the strength of one session.
That the whole-activity average of 5:33/km shows the 1 km repetitions were run faster than prescribed — the average spans a warm-up, recoveries and a cool-down.
That the cycle worked or failed.

fails_if: The answer reads a single occurrence as a trend, which is the over-correction the separation of the two claims could invite.
The answer compares a whole-session average against a repetition target as though the two were the same measurement.
The answer treats the absent activities as proof the athlete did not train, rather than as an absence nothing has resolved.
